previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with morbid obesity, steroid-dependent psoriatic arthritis, insulin-dependent diabetes, and obstructive sleep apnea was admitted from a rehabilitation facility due to recurrent episodes of hypoxemia, palpitations, and concern for pulmonary embolism. Initial evaluation ruled out new clots, but the patient had a subtherapeutic INR and a history of warfarin resistance. He was treated with heparin and carefully transitioned back to warfarin, with hematology input. Hypoxemia episodes were attributed to fluid overload and sleep apnea; he was diuresed from 386 to 366 lbs with improvement. A positive blood culture was deemed contaminated, and antibiotics were discontinued. His left leg wound showed signs of healing without active infection. A brief unresponsive episode prompted ICU evaluation and psychiatry consultation, resulting in a diagnosis of adjustment disorder with anxious features. The PICC line was removed due to safety concerns. Pain management was optimized with OxyContin and azathioprine restart. He was discharged home with services, on therapeutic anticoagulation, with follow-up arranged across multiple specialties.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ was admitted to ___ on ___ for recurrent LLE 
cellulitis. He had originally presented in ___ 
with LLE cellulitis without known source. His initial 
presentation was concerning for necrotizing fasciitis and 
required debridement (which did not identify fasciitis). He 
later developed a PE during his rehabiliation process, and has 
been repeatedly admitted for wound and cellulitic complications. 
His hospital course for this admission is summarized as follows:

1) Cellulitis - Exam on admission demonstrating cellulitis at 
proximal margin of LLE ulcer. Patient had leukocytosis but no 
other components of SIRS criteria on admission. Of note, his 
leukocytosis was likely not secondary to chronic corticosteroid 
use, as review of past records demonstrated persistently normal 
WBC depsite 4.5mg dexamethasone daily. He was started on broad 
empiric coverage with vancomycin and piperacillin-tazobactam, 
giving his recurrent admissions and diabetes. His azathioprine 
was discontinued, as his surgical wound was still failing to 
heal at a normal rate, and the wound was the most likely source 
of cellulitis. ID was consulted, and recommended transitioning 
to ceftriaxone given the Streptococcal appearance of the rash 
(rather than Staphylococcal). Mr. ___ began to improve with 
this regimen, though day to day physical exam findings 
fluctuated. He underwent a CT scan on ___ demonstrating 
multiple new fluid/air-containing collections in the 
anteromedial and medial aspect of the upper left calf, the 
largest of which measured up to 4.5 x 1.8 cm. The acute care 
surgical service was consulted. At that time no intervention was 
performed, due to patient's previous poor wound healing 
following surgical intervention; conservative management was 
indicated pending worsening or clinical deterioration. The 
patient then developed worsening pain and swelling over the next 
few days. A LLE ultrasound on ___ demonstrated large 
subcutaneous fluid collections in the cellulitic area; ACS then 
performed an I+D on the same day with significant return of 
pus-like discharge. The patient then improved significantly over 
the next several days. His pain medication requirement 
diminished as he improved. A PICC line was placed, and he was 
eventually discharged with home OPAT to continue ceftriaxone 2g 
IV daily and follow-up in ID clinc with Dr. ___ on 
___.

2) PE - Patient developed pulmonary embolism during post-op 
recovery from LLE debridement. Goal INR ___, taking 10mg and 
15mg on alternating days at admission. Warfarin held on 
admission secondary to INR of 4.5. Review of records indicates 
patient has taken widely fluctating wafarin doses (up to 42mg 
per day). No signs or symptoms of bleeding. INR on discharge 
equal to 2.3. His INR was within therpeutic range on 10mg 
warfarin per day throughout his stay. Warfarin dose on discharge 
= 10mg per day.

3) Psoriatic arthritis - On azathioprine and dexamethasone at 
home. Stopped azathioprine after discussion with outpatient 
rheumatologist. Undoubtedly contributing to poor healing of his 
ulcer. Will need follow-up with rheumatology as outpatient prior 
to starting other DMARDs.

4) DMII - Patient takes 16u qam and 33u qpm long-acting insulin 
at home. Received 16u qam, 33u qpm glargine with self-correction 
using sliding scale and carbohydrate counting. Patient very 
adept at this method of glucose control at blood sugars well 
controlled during his stay.

5) OSA - continued CPAP. Patient has frequent ventricular ectopy 
as noticed on nightly telemetry, but was cardiovascularly stable 
throughout admission.

6) HLD - Continued atorvastatin.

7) HTN - continued lisinopril.

8) PICC line safety/behavioral issues/possibility of self harm - 
Mr. ___ has multiple complex medical comorbidities as above. 
He has required multiple hospitalizations for management of 
these issues. Review of medical records identifies prior 
concerns for possible manipulation of medications and concerns 
for tampering/self-harm. Please see discharge summary in ___ 
dated ___ for further details. He has been evaluated by 
psychiatry in the past, and received a diagnosis of ""adjustment

meeting. These concerns were brought to Mr. ___ attention, 
who agreed to take medication as directed and to not tamper with 
his PICC line. Please see Dr. ___ ""Inpatient Care 
Plan"" note from ___ for further details. Tampering or 
inappropriate behavior was not directly observed on this 
admission, though the possibility of ""shaking his telemetry box 
to [create artifact looking like] v-tach"" was not able to be 
ruled out. Mr. ___ was cooperative and receptive with care 
provided on this admission. Mr. ___ and his wife received 
___ line safety teaching by a ___ staff member 
prior to discharge. He knows to let only authorized medical 
personnel access his PICC line.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  Severe left lower extremity cellulitis, in early ___
progressive necrotizing cellulitis versus fasciitis requiring debridement. 
Evaluate for fluid collection.

COMPARISON:  None available. 

FINDINGS:

No drainable fluid collection is seen surrounding the wound in the left lower
extremity medially.  No other acute abnormality is seen.  

IMPRESSION:

No drainable fluid collection

HISTORY:  Recurrent left lower extremity cellulitis at site of nonhealing
surgical ulcer with worsening edema and pain.  Evaluate for fluid collection,
abscess, or necrotizing infection.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT axial images were acquired through the left lower extremity
spanning from the proximal femur through the hindfoot during the infusion of
100 cc of intravenous Omnipaque contrast material.  Multiplanar reformats were
performed.

COMPARISON:  MR calf from ___.

FINDINGS:

There is redemonstration of moderate subcutaneous edema throughout the imaged
portion of the left lower extremity.  A soft tissue defect along the
anteromedial aspect of the left calf is similar in extent to that seen on
prior MRI.  Soft tissue attentuating material is seen subjacent to this
superficial defect, abutting the anterior margin of the posterior compartment
of the calf (2:115).  More superiorly, there are multiple fluid and air
collections within the medial and anteromedial subcutaneous tissue of the
calf, new compared to the prior MRI from ___.  The largest
collection measures 4.5 x 1.8 x 5.1 cm (series 3:88).  No definite rim
enhancement is seen.  Marked skin induration is seen along the anteromedial
aspect of the upper calf.  

There are no cortical erosions to suggest osteomyelitis.  No suspicious lytic
or blastic lesions are identified.  There is no acute fracture or dislocation.
No left knee joint effusion is seen.

Fatty atrophy of the left calf muscles is not significantly changed.

IMPRESSION:

1. Multiple new fluid/air-containing collections in the anteromedial and
medial aspect of the upper left calf, the largest of which measures up to 4.5
x 1.8 cm.  Superinfection of any or all of these collections is possible.  The
presence of a rapidly progressive infection should be assessed clinically.

2. No evidence of osteomyelitis.

3. Marked skin induration and soft tissue edema along the left lower
extremity, as described above.

CHEST RADIOGRAPH

INDICATION:  PICC line placement.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:  As compared to the previous radiograph, the patient has received a
right-sided PICC line.  The course of the line is unremarkable, the tip of the
line projects over the lower SVC.  No evidence of complications, notably no
pneumothorax.  Moderate cardiomegaly.  No pulmonary edema, no pleural
effusions radiographically determined.

HISTORY:  ___ man with cellulitis of left lower extremity status post
multiple debridements with questionable air seen on ___ CT, now with
progressive tenderness and swelling of the lateral aspect of the lytic area
concerning for worsening infection/abscess.

TECHNIQUE:  Grayscale and color Doppler evaluation of the soft tissues of the
left lower extremity.

COMPARISON:  CT left lower extremity ___.

FINDINGS:

Anterior and lateral to the patient's left lower extremity wound there is an
infiltrating fluid collection with nonmobile debris seen within it.  This
fluid collection is infiltrating and poorly defined in areas, however the
region of complex, echogenic fluid covers approximately 8 x 10 cm area.  There
is a small approximately 3 x 3 cm area of fluid at the superior medial aspect
of the wound.  The margin overlying the fluid was marked with a marker and
rotated with the letter "F".

IMPRESSION:

Subcutaneous large fluid collection at the superolateral aspect of the left
lower extremity wound with a smaller collection at the superomedial aspect of
the wound concerning for abscess in the setting of cellulitis.  The
approximate margins of the fluid were outlined and notated with the letter
"F".
